topics.topic: Existing Required-test witness bound to CLK-002
questions: Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its exclusive-reader, exact wall-reading-count, audit-reading-count, expiry-boundary, and elapsed-reading requirements?
Which existing check is the witness for CLK-002 and for the Required tests item that names it?
Which existing witness check is bound to CLK-002 and asserts its required source, counting, boundary, and viewer-entry behavior?

quotes: - Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal].
judgement.why: This is the same question about the absent CLK-002 witness binding already judged in P1, and the quoted passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Existing witness check bound to the CLK-002 requirements
quotes: - Witnesses, the focused Factory verification checks that assert it: CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal].
precedent.why: The exhaustive witness line binds both existing checks to CLK-001 and therefore answers that no existing witness check is bound to CLK-002.

topics.topic: OSV package/version matching, malformed-data handling, and fail-closed scope
questions: Which conditions make OSV data unmatchable, and does an unmatchable entry unrelated to any installed distribution fail the entire deploy or only cease to provide a verdict for a matching distribution?
What exact OSV-data conditions make the deploy check fail, and does malformed or unmatchable data unrelated to every installed distribution block the deploy?
What exact matching rule maps an installed distribution name and version to OSV packages and determines that the version is affected, including range-based entries and normalization failures?
How is an installed distribution identified and matched to an OSV PyPI package/version, and which missing, malformed, or noncanonical metadata conditions make the deploy fail closed?

quotes:
A distribution has a known vulnerability when an OSV entry that is not
   withdrawn lists its installed version as affected; reachability inside
   the portal is not judged case by case, so such a distribution blocks the
   deploy whatever feature the advisory concerns.

- DEP-002: the deploy step judges every distribution installed in the
  built image, bound to that image's content id, against the one copy of OSV
  data read in the same deploy, and starts the service only on a passing verdict about
  that same image; a listed version, unreadable or unmatchable advisory
  data, a verdict from an earlier deploy, or a verdict about another image
  does not start it
  [witness: verification:dependency_release_gate_client_portal].
judgement.divergence: One deployment gate validates the entire OSV copy and blocks on any malformed or unmatchable entry; another validates only data capable of matching an installed distribution and ignores malformed unrelated entries, so the deployment operator sees refusal versus service start.
judgement.why: The texts neither define package/version matching and normalization nor delimit which unreadable or unmatchable advisory data makes the image verdict fail closed.

witness.initial: A built image contains distributions A and B, neither affected by any valid advisory, while the copied OSV PyPI data also contains a malformed entry for unrelated distribution C.
events: The deployment procedure reads the OSV copy for the deploy.
The deployment procedure judges every distribution installed in the image and decides whether to start the service.
outcomes: The deploy does not start because the malformed unrelated entry makes the advisory data unmatchable.
The deploy starts because A and B each receive a determinate passing verdict and the unrelated malformed entry is outside the installed-distribution matching scope.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and service users.
basis:
A deploy is the start of the service from a built image. Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read once in
   that same deploy as one copy of the PyPI ecosystem data, against which
   every distribution is judged; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is
   reused.

A check that cannot
   complete does not pass: that deploy does not start the service, and a
   new deploy makes a new check.

topics.topic: Wall-clock reading timing and coverage for operations that do not use current time or refuse early
questions: Must an operation that neither writes a timestamp nor makes a current-time comparison take a wall-clock reading?
Must every portal operation take exactly one wall-clock reading, including operations that write no timestamp and make no current-time comparison, or only operations that need current time?
For every operation, including early refusals and operations that write no portal-owned timestamp, exactly when is the wall clock read, and which such invocations take no operation-level reading?

quotes:
- **Time.** Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.

authenticate_staff: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.
judgement.why: The later module rule says clock-independent operations take no wall reading, while the later operation note requires every authenticate_staff invocation, including its refusal paths, to take one operation-level reading.

topics.topic: Accepted representation and UTC normalization of source-supplied datetimes
questions: When a supplied timestamp has a non-UTC offset or is offset-aware, must the stored value be normalized to offset-naive UTC, or preserved literally in its supplied representation?
Which datetime forms are accepted for source-supplied instants, and must an offset-aware non-UTC value be normalized to naive UTC or refused?

quotes:
Times a
source supplies — `approved_at`, `published_at` of a snapshot, `confirmed_at`
of a recognition, `photo_date`, a service credential's `expires_at` — are
kept as supplied: the same instant, stored offset-naive UTC like every
persisted timestamp, never replaced by the clock (State 1 Modeling
conventions). Calendar dates a source supplies — `document_date` of a
recognition, `payment_date` — are `date` values, kept as the supplied
calendar day: they carry no time or offset, are never converted to an
instant and never replaced by the clock's day; their accepted forms and checks, and where in an operation
its one clock read happens, are the accepted spec's, carried to States 6–7.
judgement.why: This is the same source-supplied datetime representation and accepted-form question judged in P2, and the quoted passage has not changed.

quotes:

precedent.why: The passage already makes “stored as supplied” preserve the instant while normalizing storage to offset-naive UTC, while the accepted wire representations and validation checks are formats and field-type contracts owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Dependency security-review scope across direct and transitive installed distributions
questions: Does the A31 dependency-category outcome cover all distributions installed in the image, or only the requirements file and its four direct pins?
Does the security review's dependency category cover only the four direct pins, or every installed transitive distribution plus the built-image release gate required by A32?

quotes: - dependencies: APPLICABLE; references: A32; affected: deploy/requirements.txt (fastapi, pydantic, argon2-cffi, uvicorn pinned)

3. A deploy is the start of the service from a built image. Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read once in
   that same deploy as one copy of the PyPI ecosystem data, against which
   every distribution is judged; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is
   reused.
judgement.why: No passage says A31's affected-artifact list is an exhaustive definition of the distributions covered by A32 or controls the deployment verdict, so the texts do not yield two outcomes for one admissible history.

topics.topic: Verification that the designated clock source exclusively owns all host-clock access
questions: What Required test demonstrates that no other host-clock access mechanism is used, such as `os.clock_gettime`, a native binding, or an indirectly imported clock reader?
What check demonstrates that no other host-clock path—such as `os.clock_gettime`, a database time function/default, another library, or an indirect alias—reads time outside the clock source?

quotes:
- CLK-002: the clock source is the only reader of the host's wall and
  elapsed clocks; an operation takes one wall reading, and that instant
  decides every current-time comparison it makes and every portal-owned
  timestamp it writes (the audit writer's reading of `occurred_at` aside);
  the elapsed clock is read once per viewer-entry request,
  only to measure the A25 rate-limit window, and its reading is kept only
  in that window's in-memory state, never persisted, turned into an instant or ordered against a persisted record.

- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source
  imports the `time` module or calls `now`, `utcnow` or `today` of
  `datetime` or `date`, under any name, and that only the A25 viewer-entry
  rate limiter calls the elapsed reading, passing its value to no store,
  no audit and no `datetime` or `timedelta`; a test per operation that
  reads the wall clock, with a counting wall-clock source, that the
  operation takes exactly one wall reading and the audit writer one per
  appended record, and that an expiry equal to that reading is refused
  while the timestamps it writes equal that reading; and a viewer-entry
  test with a counting clock source that one request takes exactly one
  elapsed reading and that the window decision at its boundary follows
  that reading.
judgement.divergence: One verifier checks only the enumerated Python time imports and datetime/date calls and accepts an implementation that obtains time through a database default or os.clock_gettime; another verifier covers all host-clock paths and rejects it, so the State 2 invariant gate and controlled-clock tests disagree.
judgement.why: CLK-002 forbids every host-clock path, but its Required test names only selected Python imports and calls and does not say how database, native, library-mediated, or indirect clock reads are excluded.

witness.initial: An implementation calls the injected clock source once when appending an audit record but lets a database CURRENT_TIMESTAMP default supply the persisted occurred_at.
events: An owning operation asks the audit writer to append a record.
The audit writer calls the clock source once, and the database independently supplies occurred_at from its host clock.
The CLK-002 source and counting checks are run.
outcomes: A verifier limited to the enumerated imports, calls, and injected-source count passes the implementation although the database also reads a host clock.
A verifier covering database clock expressions rejects the implementation because the clock source is not the only reader and the stored occurred_at need not equal its reading.
witness.observer: The State 2 invariant gate and readers comparing the controlled clock with the persisted audit timestamp.
basis:
The one exception is the `occurred_at` of an audit record appended
through the audit writer: the writer takes it when it appends (Factory
code `application/audit_writer.py` 136); the bootstrap, which builds its
own audit, keeps its one instant.

- CLK-002: a source check that no module other than the clock source
  imports the `time` module or calls `now`, `utcnow` or `today` of
  `datetime` or `date`, under any name, and that only the A25 viewer-entry
  rate limiter calls the elapsed reading, passing its value to no store,
  no audit and no `datetime` or `timedelta`; a test per operation that
  reads the wall clock, with a counting wall-clock source, that the
  operation takes exactly one wall reading and the audit writer one per
  appended record, and that an expiry equal to that reading is refused
  while the timestamps it writes equal that reading; and a viewer-entry
  test with a counting clock source that one request takes exactly one
  elapsed reading and that the window decision at its boundary follows
  that reading.

topics.topic: Revision and completeness rules for a consistent single-copy OSV read
questions: If OSV changes while a paginated, streamed, mirrored, or otherwise multi-part read is being obtained, which revision constitutes the deploy's one copy, and when must the read be treated as incomplete?

quotes:
Before it,
   every distribution installed in that image — the pins and every library
   pip resolves for them — is checked against the OSV database (osv.dev,
   ecosystem PyPI; it aggregates the PyPA advisory database), read once in
   that same deploy as one copy of the PyPI ecosystem data, against which
   every distribution is judged; no earlier verdict or advisory copy is
   reused.

Each deploy makes one check, and its
   verdict on the one copy it read decides that deploy; an advisory added,
   changed or withdrawn after that read is judged by the next deploy.
judgement.divergence: One deployment procedure fixes the OSV revision when retrieval begins and defers advisories added during retrieval; another fixes it when retrieval completes and includes those advisories, so the deployment operator sees the same image start or be refused.
judgement.why: The rules assign each deploy one OSV copy but do not define the read boundary or consistency revision for a streamed, paginated, or mirrored retrieval.

witness.initial: Image I contains distribution D version V, and OSV initially contains no advisory affecting it.
events: The deployment procedure begins retrieving the PyPI ecosystem data.
OSV adds a non-withdrawn advisory affecting D version V before retrieval finishes.
The deployment procedure finishes retrieval and judges image I.
outcomes: The advisory is after the deploy's read boundary, belongs to the next deploy, and image I starts.
The advisory is inside the deploy's completed copy, so image I is refused.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users waiting for image I to start.
basis: A deploy is the start of the service from a built image.

Each deploy makes one check, and its
   verdict on the one copy it read decides that deploy; an advisory added,
   changed or withdrawn after that read is judged by the next deploy.

questions: Which later state owns the concrete image enumeration, single-copy OSV acquisition, image-content binding, and service-start gate, and which check confirms that execution?

topics.topic: Whether withdrawn OSV advisories still block deployment
questions: Does a withdrawn OSV entry that still lists the installed version as affected block deployment?

quotes:
A distribution has a known vulnerability when an OSV entry that is not
   withdrawn lists its installed version as affected; reachability inside
   the portal is not judged case by case, so such a distribution blocks the
   deploy whatever feature the advisory concerns.
judgement.why: This is the same withdrawn-advisory question already judged in P4, and the quoted passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether withdrawn OSV advisories still block deployment
quotes:
A distribution has a known vulnerability when an OSV entry that is not
   withdrawn lists its installed version as affected; reachability inside
   the portal is not judged case by case, so such a distribution blocks the
   deploy whatever feature the advisory concerns.
precedent.why: The normative definition expressly excludes withdrawn OSV entries, so an affected-version entry marked withdrawn does not constitute the known vulnerability forbidden by DEP-002.
